question: A triangle in the coordinate plane has vertices \(A(\log_2 1, \log_2 2),\) \(B(\log_2 3, \log_2 4),\) and \(C(\log_2 7, \log_2 8).\) What is the area of \(\triangle ABC?\)
solution:
The three vertical coordinates are \(1,2,3\), so the horizontal line through \(B\) lies halfway between \(A\) and \(C\). This gives two triangles with especially simple heights.

Let \(u=\log_2 3\) and \(v=\log_2 7\). Evaluating the other logarithms gives
\[
A=(0,1),\qquad B=(u,2),\qquad C=(v,3).
\]
The midpoint \(M\) of \(AC\) is \((v/2,2)\), so \(BM\) is horizontal. Since
\[
2u-v=\log_2\frac97>0,
\]
point \(B\) lies to the right of \(M\), and
\[
BM=u-\frac v2.
\]
Segment \(BM\) splits \(ABC\) into triangles \(ABM\) and \(CBM\). Each has base \(BM\) and height \(1\), because \(A\) and \(C\) lie one unit below and above the line \(y=2\). Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
[ABC]
&=\frac12 BM+\frac12 BM\\
&=u-\frac v2\\
&=\log_2 3-\log_2\sqrt7\\
&=\log_2\frac3{\sqrt7}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The area is \(\boxed{\log_2\frac3{\sqrt7}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).

solutionMethods.explanation:
Evaluating the logarithms of powers of \(2\) makes the vertical coordinates integers, leaving a short shoelace calculation.

Set \(u=\log_2 3\) and \(v=\log_2 7\). The vertices are
\[
A=(0,1),\qquad B=(u,2),\qquad C=(v,3).
\]
The shoelace formula gives the triangle's area as half the absolute difference of the cyclic coordinate products:
\[
\begin{aligned}
[ABC]
&=\frac12\left|0\cdot2+u\cdot3+v\cdot1
-\bigl(1\cdot u+2\cdot v+3\cdot0\bigr)\right|\\
&=\frac12|2u-v|.
\end{aligned}
\]
By the logarithm rules,
\[
2u-v=\log_2\frac97>0.
\]
Thus
\[
[ABC]=\frac12\log_2\frac97
=\log_2\sqrt{\frac97}
=\log_2\frac3{\sqrt7}.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{\log_2\frac3{\sqrt7}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
solutionMethods.label: Apply the coordinate area formula
